name: Dutasteride on cycle (dut on cycle)

card.summary: Using the 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor dutasteride during anabolic-steroid or testosterone use to reduce DHT-driven hair loss and keep a full head of hair.
card.note: Prescription drug with sexual and other side effects; off-label for this use.

quick.overview:
Dut on cycle refers to taking dutasteride, a prescription drug that blocks the conversion of testosterone to DHT, while using androgens, so as to protect the scalp hair that DHT can thin in people predisposed to male pattern baldness. Keeping hair is the appearance payoff.

Dutasteride is approved for prostate enlargement in the US and for male pattern hair loss in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan. Its use alongside anabolic steroids has not been studied in trials; discussion comes from forums.
quick.how: Forum users describe adding a 5-ARI such as finasteride or dutasteride to hormone use, sometimes plus minoxidil or topical products. The route can be oral or topical. Specific amounts are not covered here.
quick.risks: Reported effects include erectile dysfunction, lower libido, breast enlargement and a boxed warning for high-grade prostate cancer risk; persistence after stopping is debated. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and has a half-life of weeks. Forum users have also reported stopping it after sexual symptoms.

lead: Dutasteride on cycle is a looksmaxxing and bodybuilding practice in which people using testosterone or anabolic steroids also take dutasteride to guard against hair loss. Dutasteride inhibits all three 5-alpha-reductase isoforms, which convert testosterone to DHT, the androgen linked to pattern baldness.[1]

It can lower blood DHT by up to 98 percent, versus 65 to 70 percent for finasteride, which is the reason cited for its stronger hair effects.[1] It is FDA-approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia (2001), and approved for hair loss in South Korea (2009), Japan (2015) and Taiwan (2016); elsewhere hair use is off-label.[1]

On T Nation, one poster states that testosterone plus a 5-ARI such as finasteride or dutasteride is the most effective approach among those discussed.[2] No trials have tested dutasteride specifically in people using anabolic steroids.

chain: Less testosterone converted to scalp DHT
angle.text: People on androgens use it to protect hairline and density from DHT-related thinning.

paras: Androgens, including testosterone and some steroids, raise exposure to DHT in scalp tissue in genetically susceptible users. 5-ARIs reduce DHT; finasteride inhibits types II and III while dutasteride inhibits I, II and III.[1][3]
Forum users on T Nation discuss pairing a 5-ARI with cycles, with some asking about topical dutasteride and minoxidil to limit systemic DHT reduction.[4][5]

In a study of 6,729 men with BPH, erectile dysfunction occurred in 9 percent (vs 5.7 percent placebo), decreased libido in 3.3 percent and breast enlargement in 1.9 percent.[1] Sexual dysfunction is estimated at 3.4 to 15.8 percent for finasteride or dutasteride, and may persist in some men after stopping.[3] The FDA added a boxed warning in 2011 about high-grade prostate cancer risk.[1]
A T Nation user reported stopping dutasteride after a year when ED symptoms appeared, expecting them to clear in weeks.[6]

No studies found on its use alongside androgen or anabolic-steroid regimens. Registered trials of dutasteride address prostate conditions, such as a 4,844-person phase 3 trial combining dutasteride with tamsulosin for BPH.[7]

timeline.event: US FDA approves dutasteride for BPH.[1]
South Korea approves it for male pattern hair loss.[1]
Japan approves it for hair loss; US patent expires.[1]

lore.intro: On T Nation, hair protection during androgen use is a frequent topic, with 5-ARIs, minoxidil and topical agents compared.[2][4][5]

claims.claim: Testosterone plus a 5-ARI is the most effective way to protect hair on cycle.
claims.believers: A poster says these drugs work and that finasteride is FDA approved for male pattern baldness.[2]
claims.experts: Dutasteride lowers DHT more than finasteride and is approved for hair loss in several Asian countries; no trials cover steroid users.[1]

claims.claim: Dutasteride can cause sexual side effects.
claims.believers: One user described ED symptoms after a year of use and stopped.[6]
claims.experts: Trial data in BPH show higher rates of ED and reduced libido than placebo.[1]
